title: Gun only option: Mountie; Officer testifies at inquest into shooting death of Holdfast man
article: The RCMP officer involved in the 2013 shooting death of 42-yearold Gerald Lord in Holdfast told a coroner's jury he had no choice but to use his firearm.

"It was the only option I felt like I could use at this point," said the officer, who can only be identified as Const. Eric due to a publication ban. The ban, the jury was told, has nothing to do with the incident, but rather unrelated police work in which he is currently involved.
The officer - a three-year member stationed at the Craik detachment at the time of the Sept. 11, 2013, incident - testified Monday at a coroner's inquest into Lord's death.

During sometimes-emotional testimony, Eric said he was the lone on-duty member at his detachment when he received a complaint from Holdfast resident Harry Fischer about Lord, a former friend of Fischer's. Fischer reported Lord was repeatedly texting and calling him, accusing him of stealing a hammer. Lord sounded intoxicated, Fischer had said.

After attending Fischer's residence - a visit punctuated by approximately 10 calls from Lord, Eric said - the officer went over to Lord's to speak with him, believing he had the grounds to lay a charge of criminal harassment. A check on the system revealed no warrants or concerns about violence in relation to Lord.

The situation quickly went downhill, Lord just "staring blank" when he came to the door, Eric said. The officer noted Lord was significantly larger than he was, estimating he outweighed him by almost 100 pounds.
Eric said Lord didn't respond to attempts to speak with him and tried to close the door once Eric, concerned about Lord's demeanour, advised him he was under arrest.
Eric managed to get a foot in the door and one of Lord's wrists in a handcuff, he said, adding he tried to use pressure point tactics to gain control of the non-compliant man.

Eric said Lord then grabbed his collar and the strap of his Kevlar vest, pushing the officer against the wall in a small, darkened entry area just inside the rear door. A struggle ensued during which Eric said Lord got both hands up around his collar and throat area, and the officer said he worried he would be choked by the chain of the handcuffs he had managed to snap fully into place.
"I couldn't move either way," he said. "He had control of me."
Lord, he said, looked "angry" and was yelling, "Get out of my house or I'll kill you."

Eric said he repeatedly told Lord to let him go to no avail, and was unable to use pepper spray or his expandable baton because of the close quarters and the risk to himself. Eric said he tried using his Taser but it had no effect.

He said he began losing his balance and was pushed down on his back onto a set of stairs leading up to a kitchen area. With the larger man on top, hands still in the area of his throat, the officer said he feared for his life.
"I had to do something else just to stay alive," he said.
Eric said he drew his sidearm and fired two shots, though the way he was being held prevented him from seeing where they impacted. Lord, he said, loosened his
grip for a moment but then came at him again, so Eric aimed for Lord's head. Eric then reported the death to dispatch and a senior officer.
Just four minutes passed between Eric's arrival at the home and his report of shots fired.
The inquest, being heard at Regina Court of Queen's Bench, is set to continue for the rest of the week.
